newsitem.title: FRANCE: French drivers' strike hits dozen provincial towns.
newsitem.headline: French drivers' strike hits dozen provincial towns.

text.p: A strike by drivers severely disrupted and in some cases halted public transport in a dozen provincial French towns on Friday in the latest stoppage called to press demands for earlier retirement and shorter working hours.
Unions and officials said Clermont-Ferrand, Dijon, Quimper, Brest and Colmar were among towns hit by protests called by the Communist CGT and the non-partisan Force Ouvriere (FO) unions.

In Dijon, transport authorities said 40 percent of drivers had heeded the strike call and that strikers were blocking bus depots, preventing any services. In Clermont-Ferrand, where strikes entered their 23rd day, only 17 out of 140 buses were running.
Unions are demanding retirement at 55 instead of 60 years, and a cut in working hours to 35 per week.

In a separate dispute, the CGT and FO said on Thursday that hospital personnel would step up their protests against austerity measures in the health budget, with a likely day of nationwide strikes and protests in mid-March.
According to FO, the cuts imposed by the centre-right government as part of welfare reforms will mean the loss of 15,000 to 20,000 jobs in hospitals.
